UXM266:

One of the biggest problems in comics now is trying to introduce new characters, and places. For the most part they don't fare well. They either get called redundant for being too similar to something else, such as a teenage-this, or a female-version-that, or these-IN-SPACE, or those-but-alternate-uiverse.

Did you intend for those to be the only "ors" there?

You can't add a new location simply because it's new. It has to be different enough to be interesting

I totally disagree.  I would love to have Environments for cities other than Megalopolis or Rook City (Silver Gulch doesn't count)…one of the current SCUverse games had to be set in Time Cataclysm because it was the closet I could get to a "generic" setting, and I'd already used MP two games before and was saving RC for a game or two thereafter.

The good thing about having only a set few of tools is that writers and artists don't need to constantly create, new worlds, and explain what they are to the heroes, why they should be there, how they got there and what it is. Doing something new without explaining WHY or HOW is a risky move in the comic book industry.

They wouldn't have to explain if the characters went off to fight crime in some real-world location; no explanation is needed for anything that actually exists.  That they're better off not making up too many strange new dimensions, that I do agree, but too many people dismiss the Earth as an ordinary and boring place…in actuality, our homeworld contains a mind-boggling breadth of diversity, and I'd love to see more comics Do The Research and engage in vicarious tourism of the many fascinating places worldwide.  Imagine a comics issue taking place on the slopes of Macchu Pichu, or in the Scottish highlands, or the coast of Cozumel, or a remote African village of subsistence farmers with a unique tribal culture.  Sometimes these could just be backdrop for super-battles, but other times they could be the focus of stories where the superheroes take time to connect with ordinary people, and solve problems that don't just involve punching something at lightspeed.

Random thoughts after reading this thread...

While a bunch of new mini-Expansion Environments would be cool, what percentage of Sentinels players would buy them? The people posting in this thread would. I would (I'm a horribly-crazy completionist when I love something). But would the more casual Sentinels players? probably not. There's likely a point (which we may already be at) where it wouldn't make financial sense for them to do Environment expansions. Villains and (especially) Heroes, yes. Environments, eh...

I do kinda like the mix and match setting + theme generic Environment theme. I think it has some real potential.

On the other hand, what makes the existing Environments so cool is how flavorful, detailed, and specific they are.

Someone (I'm too lazy/tired to scroll back up) said that there are several Heroes w/o Nemesis Villains yet. I do believe (since I was looking at this while building a list of battles I'd like to fight) that there are six. Given the 2H + 4V + 2E pattern of most of the expansions, we'd need a minimum of three more to complete the Hero-Villain match-ups, providing the 6 new Heroes all had their Nemesis Villains within the 12 new Villains.

Sure we'd all love 100 Heroes, 100 Villains, & 100 Environments, but the poor, sad, gamers out there that haven't discovered Sentinels would be overwealmed.

Official Environment expansions would be cool, but there's nothing inherently wrong with a <strong>well done</strong> fan built one. I'm looking forward to trying Spiff's space station one as soon as I replace my printer. (You do not want to know what the cats did to the old printer.)

I think I had several other thoughts but they seem to have gotten bord and wandered off...

--MIchael
